why: Both cover the room answering trouble to its work, and the items here mix calls to fight back with reports of covered tiles and repairs, so the line between an attack fought and a work watched and fixed is the one to watch.

why.T3-009: The item's concepts mostly mark the finished work as achieved and enjoyable (one logo survived to the end, a good thing going, a good time, fun while it lasted), so it is celebrating the work rather than reporting how it fared (T3-073) or mourning it (T3-029).

why.T3-001: The room stages its own fake season-release and its members reveal, improve and play along with it, satisfying staging April Fools fake news rather than testing an outside claim (T3-095) or reacting to an official joke (T3-048).

why.T3-054: One concept sends members to rebuild on another pixel canvas (r/pxlsspace), which is taking up a later canvas of the same kind, not remaking the work in another medium (T3-057) or moving to a new spot on the same canvas (T3-022).

why.T3-098: A member asks what the room's mark The R is, questioning the room's showing on the canvas, rather than explaining what r/place is (T3-016) or decoding a finished picture's detail (T3-018).

why.T3-003: Members report their own last pixels and logos placed before the canvas ended, telling their own placing labour, which is narrower than registering that the canvas has ended (T3-117) or celebrating the finished work (T3-009).

why.T3-156: Members want flairs made for the R campaign and one takes up the work, taking the mark into the sub's identity as a flair, rather than a rules change (T3-185) which is about what may be posted.

why.T3-065: The leading act is getting the room's own land flag onto the canvas (call to build it, proportions, first pixels placed), so the flag itself is the mark; the calls for hands and the coordinates/templates that carry it have concepts of their own under T3-002 and T3-070.

why.T3-174: The room's own members hail their mark and cause with slogans (freedom will prevail, long live the R), professing loyalty to the room's symbol rather than cheering someone else's faction (T3-096) or just playing the room's in-joke (T3-031).

why.T3-005: The leading concepts rally the logos against an attack under way (fight back the purple, report the invasion, call for help while under attack); the choice to spare and combine with the rainbow road is a separate kind of restraint with its own concepts under T3-024.

why.T3-041: The proposals add new pieces and inscriptions beside the working logo plan, extending the room's work rather than proposing the room's first mark (T3-033) or settling the chosen mark's own look (T3-004).

why.T3-001: The room stages its own fake season-release and its members reveal, improve and play along with it, satisfying staging April Fools fake news rather than testing an outside claim (T3-095) or judging an official joke (T3-048).

why.T3-005: The room is dedicated to and called on to protect its great R, keeping the room's mark safe; with defence as the stated point it sits with defending the work rather than a bare call for hands to build (T3-002).

why.T3-004: Most concepts work out the logo's look (image, measurements, smaller version, shrinking, black-then-figure), settling the mark's design; the concepts choosing a site (void, quiet patch, ignoreable area) have their own footing under T3-020.

why.T3-002: The leading concepts call the room's people in and offer to place (recruit r/blackmirror, ask for the official location, ask for help with the wall), which is calling members in to place; the doubts about numbers have their own concepts under T3-136.
